about:
Sana Packaging operates from Denver, Colorado, specializing in full-service cannabis packaging. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or the names of its founders.

The company produces a range of cannabis packaging including jars, bottles, and flexible pouches made from post-consumer recycled (PCR) plastic and reclaimed ocean-bound plastic. Its capabilities encompass extrusion and molding, label printing and application, direct printing, in-mold labeling, custom flexible pouches, and custom paperboard displays. Sana Packaging reports having reclaimed over 768,000 pounds of ocean-bound plastic and maintains on-hand inventory with low minimum order quantities for stock items.

Sana Packaging serves the cannabis industry, supplying dispensaries, brands, and cultivators with child-resistant, FDA-compliant packaging that meets regulatory requirements. The company also partners with HempPress and Tree Hugger Containers to offer additional product lines, all warehoused and shipped from domestic locations.

The company differentiates itself through a 'no silly business, no hidden fees, and no BS' policy, emphasizing transparent pricing, quick turnaround times, and sustainability. It highlights responsible material sourcing, waste-reducing design, and end-of-life recoverability as core to its approach, alongside next-business-day shipping for blank in-stock products.

name: Sandbox VT
old_description: The SANDBOX is a no-bounds creators space that promotes sustainable action through creativity, community and curated experiences based in the south end of Burlington, VT.
about:
Sandbox VT is based in the south end of Burlington, Vermont, where it runs a repair and circular services operation from a storefront The venture began as a creators space promoting sustainable action through creativity and community, though the exact founding year and ownership structure are not specified in public materials.

The business provides a range of textile repair and restoration services for both individuals and commercial clients. For consumers, offerings include clothing repair, technical outerwear and gear repair, backpack repair, zipper replacement, alterations, and a mail‑in repair option. For brands, retailers, and designers, Sandbox VT runs warranty and repair programs, provides overflow repair capacity, performs technical sewing, product restoration, waterproofing, returns refurbishment, and executes small‑batch production runs using upcycled brand sample fabric. The company also curates a monthly marketplace of gently pre‑loved apparel.

Clients span individual consumers seeking to extend the life of personal garments, as well as outdoor brands, retailers, and designers who prioritize durability and circularity. The company explicitly mentions working with outdoor brands and retailers that believe in quality and doing better, and it serves designers needing small‑batch production from sample materials.

Sandbox VT states its mission is to make repair the first choice, extending the life of clothing and gear through expert repair, restoration, and circular services to keep products in use longer and out of the waste stream.

name: Sander's Sew-N-Vac + The Fabric Bin
about:
Sander's Sew-N-Vac + The Fabric Bin operates from a downtown storefront in Aberdeen, South Dakota. The business traces its roots to 1945 when Al Sander opened Sander's Sew-N-Vac to sell Electrolux vacuums. In 1976 his son Greg Sander purchased the shop and, in the late 1990s, expanded into fabric retail under the name The Fabric Bin. The company remains a family-owned proprietorship, now managed by Greg with support from longtime employees Shirelle Stadel and Alesha Stadel.

The store carries hundreds of bolts of fabric alongside notions, pre-cut kits, and sewing supplies, and also runs an e‑commerce site with live‑streamed shopping events. In‑store services include weekly live shows, sewing classes, and personalized project assistance. The physical location is open Tuesday through Saturday with limited hours, and the business offers 0% interest financing through a third‑party partner.

Customers are primarily hobbyists, quilters, and home sewers looking for fabric yardage, specialty notions, and guided project kits. The shop serves both walk‑in traffic in the Aberdeen area and online buyers across the United States.

Greg Sander has said the business exists to continue his father’s vision of keeping the Sander name on Main Street while providing a hands‑on resource for the local sewing community. The emphasis on personal service, education, and a curated fabric selection is presented as the core reason customers return.

old_description: Our portfolio of brands help nourish people around the world.
about:
Wayne-Sanderson Farms is headquartered in Collins, Mississippi. The company was formed from two poultry companies with humble roots, bringing together over a century of industry expertise.

The company produces high-quality, affordable poultry brands and products, operating as the nation's third-largest poultry producer. Its network includes more than 26,000 team members and over 2,000 family farmers. Operations emphasize efficient production, resource conservation, renewable energy, and waste reduction.

Wayne-Sanderson Farms serves customers and consumers worldwide, supplying retail, foodservice, and institutional markets. Notable partnerships include being named the official chicken of the Southeastern Conference and collaborations with professional athletes such as LPGA golfer Jenny Bae, whose family has raised chickens for the company for a decade.

name: Sandridge Crafted Foods
old_description: Where does your operation fit in? Select an option below for a personalized experience.
about:
Sandridge Crafted Foods traces its roots to 1960 when Vincent R. Sandridge began selling vacuum-packed deli meats in Cuyahoga Falls, Ohio. The company, now headquartered in Morton, Illinois, remains a third-generation, family-owned operation. Vincent’s son Mark D. Sandridge joined in 1976, later purchasing the business in 1997 and expanding into kettle-cooked soups, sauces, and sous vide proteins. Today, Mark’s sons Jordan and Dane serve as co-presidents, steering the business alongside nearly 1,000 employees across multiple facilities.

The company produces chef-crafted fresh foods including deli salads, soups, sauces, sous vide proteins, and assembled meal kits. Core technologies include high-pressure processing (HPP) for preservative-free shelf-life extension, European-inspired kettle cooking for layered flavors, and precision sous vide cooking. A 2023-opened Center of Excellence in Medina, Ohio, houses a culinary R&D team that runs a “bench-to-box” development process. Facilities also feature blanching systems, vegetable prep lines, and cold-chain logistics managed through sister company MDS Inc.

Sandridge serves college and university dining, deli and prepared-food retailers, foodservice distributors, and healthcare operators. Its branded lines—Grandma’s®, Melch’s®, and the new Simply Crafted™—appear in retail and foodservice channels, while private-label and co-pack programs supply custom formulations for national and regional brands.

The founding vision centered on fresh, authentic food that fosters community. Leadership emphasizes culinary innovation backed by food-science rigor, a GFSI/SQFI-certified safety program, and a vertically integrated cold chain to deliver “remarkably fresh” products without artificial preservatives.

name: Sands Electric Co
old_description: Founded in 1896. Sands Electric has been supplying the Upper Ohio Valley for over 115 years.
about:
Sands Electric Co. has operated from Wheeling, West Virginia since its founding in 1896. The company remains family owned and operated, serving as an electrical wholesale distributor for the Upper Ohio Valley region. Over more than a century, it has built a reputation as a steady supplier for electrical contractors and industrial buyers in the tri-state area.

As a wholesale distributor, Sands Electric stocks thousands of electrical products from industry brands. The company operates from a location at 52 18th Street in Wheeling, maintaining business hours Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Its inventory spans wire, conduit, lighting, controls, and related electrical supplies sourced from major manufacturers.

The distributor supplies customers across the Upper Ohio Valley, providing electrical materials to contractors, industrial facilities, and commercial projects in the region. Its customer base includes electrical contractors, maintenance departments, and OEMs requiring reliable access to branded electrical components.

The company's longevity and family ownership underscore its focus on consistent supply and local service for electrical professionals in West Virginia and surrounding areas.

name: Sandtown Furniture Co.
old_description: Customize your specs & fill out the Contact Form below. We'll get you a quote in a day.
about:
Sandtown Furniture Co. operates from Baltimore, Maryland, where it salvages lumber from the city’s own streets and structures and transforms it into commercial furniture. The company is led by partner and head designer James Battaglia, who oversees design and production. While a founding year is not publicly disclosed, the business began with a mission to give Baltimore’s reclaimed wood a second life as functional pieces.

The shop produces board room tables, conference and communal tables, restaurant and cafe tables, architectural millwork, credenzas, and storage units. All pieces are designed and built in-house, using reclaimed wood sourced locally. The operation includes custom milling, joinery, and finishing, with hardware such as push-to-open door mechanisms and adjustable shelving integrated into the designs. Facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Sandtown serves commercial offices, hospitality venues, and architectural firms. Its tables and millwork have been specified for boardrooms, collaborative workspaces, and restaurant dining areas. The company also works directly with designers and architects on custom architectural millwork projects.

The company distinguishes itself by sourcing all lumber from within Baltimore, emphasizing the character of the reclaimed material. It also operates an event venue, The Butterfly Room, at its HQ2 location, reflecting a broader community focus. Custom specifications are quoted within one day.

Sanford Health Equip Bismarck operates a retail location Suite C, in Bismarck, North Dakota. The store is part of Sanford Health Equip, which provides durable medical equipment and health care accessories across the region. The Bismarck outlet is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The location stocks a broad inventory of home medical products, including bathroom safety items, CPAP machines and supplies, home respiratory and oxygen equipment, incontinence products, wheelchair and mobility aids, lift chair recliners, power scooters, orthotics and prosthetics, mastectomy clothing, breast pumps, compression garments, nutritional supplies, skin and wound care products, and women's specialty items. Staff work with customers to find the proper fit and services for their conditions and lifestyles.

The business serves individual patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers in the Bismarck area who require durable medical equipment for home use. Its product range addresses needs in post-surgical recovery, chronic respiratory conditions, mobility limitations, and women's health.

Sanford Health Equip states its mission is to empower customers to regain independence and make everyday life easier through high-quality products and personalized service.

name: Sanko Gosei Technologies USA, Inc.
old_description: Full-service Injection Molding 200 Ton through 3500 Ton Capacity
about:
Sanko Gosei Technologies USA, Inc. operates a manufacturing facility in Fort Wayne, Indiana, serving as the U.S. arm of a global organization focused on thermoplastic injection molding. The company runs over 40 injection molding machines with clamping forces ranging from 200 to 3,500 tons, supported by a workforce of approximately 180 employees. This equipment base enables production of a wide variety of plastic components with flexibility across part sizes and complexities.

The facility specializes in thermoplastic injection molding for automotive applications, producing components for vehicle manufacturers and tier suppliers. Its technical expertise is built on experience across multiple sectors, though automotive remains the core market highlighted in its public materials. The company emphasizes advanced machinery and systems to maintain a competitive edge in delivery and design support.

Sanko Gosei Technologies USA positions continuous investment in state-of-the-art equipment and highly skilled professionals as its primary differentiator. This strategy aims to tackle manufacturing challenges, reduce costs, and enhance part designs for customers. The company describes its approach as mastering cutting-edge technology to deliver tailored solutions that meet evolving automotive industry demands.
